title: Eisenstein’s facades
episode: Mikhail Eisenstein: The Man Behind Riga's Art Nouveau | Albert Street & UNESCO Heritage
description: On Mikhail Eisenstein, the city engineer who designed some of Riga’s most extravagant Art Nouveau facades around 1900, full of screaming faces and peacocks. His son Sergei, born in Riga in 1898, directed Battleship Potemkin.

title: Baryshnikov’s Riga
episode: Baryshnikov on Riga and the Opera
description: Mikhail Baryshnikov, born in Riga in 1948, on the city where he grew up and first trained as a dancer before leaving for Leningrad.

title: A market in zeppelin hangars
episode: Inside Riga's Old Zeppelin Hangars | Historic Market & Traditional Baltic Foods
description: Riga’s Central Market, one of the largest in Europe, opened in 1930 in five hangars built for German zeppelins in the First World War and moved here from western Latvia.

title: The Freedom Monument unveiled
episode: Brivibas pieminekla atklasana 1935  Freedom Monument  Unveil
description: Footage of November 18, 1935, when the Freedom Monument, paid for by public donations, was unveiled. The Soviets left it standing, and in the late 1980s it became the rallying point of the independence movement.
